canonical_statement: For two densely defined self-adjoint observables A and B on a complex Hilbert space and a normalized vector psi in both domains and both operator-product domains, the product of their standard deviations is at least half the norm of the expected commutator. For Q and P satisfying [Q,P]x = i*hbar*x on their common product domain, with hbar nonnegative, this specializes to Delta(Q) Delta(P) >= hbar/2.
domain_and_universes: universe u; H : Type u; NormedAddCommGroup H; InnerProductSpace Complex H; each observable contains a complex submodule domain, a linear map from that domain, and density of the domain; target is Prop
ordered_binders: A B (or Q P) : Observable H
hypotheses: psi lies in both operator domains
B psi lies in A's domain and A psi lies in B's domain
0 <= hbar and the canonical commutation relation for the specialization
conclusion: The Robertson lower bound and its hbar/2 canonical-commutation specialization.
minimal_import_evidence: The sole direct import supplies complex inner-product spaces, dense subsets, submodules, norms, and inner products. No adjoint, matrix, spectral, probability, or legacy Stage1 module is imported.
encoding_boundary: Pinned mathlib has no identified native densely-defined unbounded-operator/adjoint interface. Observable records a dense submodule and a linear action on it. IsSelfAdjoint states symmetry plus equality of the operator domain with the domain characterized by existence of an adjoint value; it contains no uncertainty inequality. Any future native encoding needs a checked transport.

degenerate_cases: Zero deviation and hbar = 0 remain in scope. No finite-dimensionality, nonzero commutator, positive hbar, or everywhere-definedness premise is added. Product-domain witnesses make both AB psi and BA psi well typed.
